| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_hash IN ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba","90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59","2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba","c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | append [ | tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba","90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59","2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba","c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") OR Filesystem.file_name IN ("VID001.exe","u112417.dat","APQ9305.dll") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` ] | sort - lastTime
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",

   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"

SecurityEvent

| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'

      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.

ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental

        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'

falsepositives:

level: critical
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.process_hash IN ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process_hash
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]

Portainer Swarm service create/update API access (CVE-2026-44849 exploitation path) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts for HTTP POST traffic to the Portainer Docker Swarm service create / update endpoints that the CVE-2026-44849 advisory identifies as the bypass surface. Surfaces the specific URI paths (/services/create and /services/{id}/update) that skip EndpointSecuritySettings validation so analysts can pivot to who exercised them and from where. Rationale: Targets the two URIs the GHSA explicitly names as the bypass surface (POST /services/create with 1-of-7 checks, POST /services/{id}/update with 0-of-7 checks, plus POST /volumes/create which never had the bind-mount check). Pivots on the exact paths from the advisory so signal is bound to the vulnerable endpoints rather than generic Docker API noise. Cross-referenced with Portainer release notes (2.33.8 / 2.39.2 / 2.41.0). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/portainer/portainer/releases • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w
ATT&CKT1190 T1078.003
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Administrator legitimately creating new Swarm services through the Portainer UI
  • Automation pipelines (Ansible / Terraform / GitOps) calling Portainer API to deploy stacks
  • Portainer agent health-checks polling Swarm endpoints
  • CI runners updating service images via portainer-cli or curl as part of release deploys
Suppression filter
| where csUserName !endswith "$" and csUserName !in~ ("portainer-agent", "system", "automation-svc")
| where csUserAgent !has_any ("terraform", "ansible", "gitops")
Response runbook
1) Triage: Pull the user that issued the POST (csUserName / InitiatingProcessAccountName) and check whether they are an admin role in Portainer. Non-admin users with Swarm endpoint access are the at-risk population. Pull the request body if your proxy logs it; look for CapabilityAdd, Privileges.Seccomp.Mode=unconfined, or Mounts with type=volume + DriverConfig.Options. 2) Contain: Temporarily revoke Swarm endpoint access for non-admin Portainer users via Portainer RBAC (per advisory workaround). If a malicious service is identified, force-delete it and quarantine the node it landed on. 3) Hunt: Pivot the source IP and user against successful authentications to Portainer, then look for downstream container processes that spawned chroot, nsenter, or accessed /var/run/docker.sock — see related UCs.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/services/create", "/volumes/create")
   or RemoteUrl matches regex @"/services/[^/]+/update"
| where RemotePort in (9000, 9443, 8000, 443)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Hits = count(), AnyCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl
| order by LastSeen desc
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod =~ "POST"
| where csUriStem has_any ("/services/create", "/volumes/create")
   or csUriStem matches regex @"/services/[^/]+/update"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Hits = count(), Methods = make_set(csMethod), URIs = make_set(csUriStem)
           by Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csUserName, csUserAgent
| order by LastSeen desc

Portainer Swarm service spec with elevated Linux capabilities or unconfined Seccomp AIExploitation High
Hunts for the docker daemon on a Swarm-enabled host receiving service specs that contain the privileged values the CVE-2026-44849 advisory describes (CapabilityAdd: SYS_ADMIN/NET_ADMIN/SYS_PTRACE/ALL, Privileges.Seccomp.Mode: unconfined, AppArmor disabled). Captures the daemon-side artefact of the bypass even when proxy logs don't include request bodies. Rationale: Pulls the exact capability strings (SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, ALL) and modes (unconfined Seccomp, disabled AppArmor) listed in the GHSA Impact section. These values are not part of normal container spec on most fleets, so the binding to dockerd/containerd/runc plus those specific tokens keeps FP rate low. Verified against the advisory's pre-fix code excerpt showing CapabilityAdd/Sysctls/Privileges were never parsed by the partial service struct. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/service/create/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
ATT&CKT1611 T1610 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate privileged workloads (CNI plugins, eBPF agents, observability daemonsets) that genuinely need CAP_SYS_ADMIN
  • Security-tool deployments (Falco, sysdig, tetragon) launched with cap_net_admin or cap_sys_ptrace
  • Kubernetes / Swarm operator pre-deploying privileged init containers for storage drivers
  • Penetration-test or red-team exercises explicitly authorised to test capability assignment
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("falco", "sysdig", "tetragon", "cilium-agent")
| where ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("kube-system", "calico-node", "weave-net")
Response runbook
1) Triage: Identify which Portainer user (cross-ref UC1) or which orchestrator deployed the service. Pull the docker inspect output for the running container — confirm whether CapabilityAdd/Privileges actually contain the elevated values vs being passed but rejected. 2) Contain: docker service rm the offending service (or kubectl delete if K8s-managed). Block the Portainer user's session and rotate their credentials. If the container had bind-mount of /, treat the host as potentially compromised. 3) Hunt: Sweep the same host for chroot/nsenter activity (UC3) and for write events under /etc, /root/.ssh, /var/spool/cron, or /usr/local/sbin (persistence). Pull docker.sock access events on the host (UC4).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2")
   or FileName in~ ("runc", "crun", "containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("CAP_SYS_ADMIN", "CAP_NET_ADMIN", "CAP_SYS_PTRACE", "cap_sys_admin", "cap_net_admin", "cap_sys_ptrace", "\"ALL\"", "seccomp=unconfined", "apparmor=unconfined", "AppArmorProfile=unconfined", "\"Mode\":\"unconfined\"")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "portainer", "runc", "crun")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("CAP_SYS_ADMIN", "CAP_NET_ADMIN", "CAP_SYS_PTRACE", "cap_sys_admin", "cap_net_admin", "cap_sys_ptrace", "seccomp=unconfined", "apparmor=unconfined", "\"unconfined\"", "\"capabilities\":[\"ALL\"]", "CapabilityAdd")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage, HostIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Docker Swarm Service Spec With Elevated Capabilities or Unconfined Seccomp (CVE-2026-44849)
id: 3c5c9f9a-5f6e-4b6a-9c5a-44849aaa0002
description: Detects dockerd / containerd / runc receiving service specs with elevated Linux capabilities or seccomp/apparmor unconfined, the post-bypass artefact of CVE-2026-44849.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w
author: SOC Detection Engineering

detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/dockerd'
      - '/containerd'
      - '/runc'
      - '/crun'
      - '/containerd-shim-runc-v2'
  selection_args:

      - 'CAP_SYS_ADMIN'

level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog OR docker) (@process.name:(dockerd OR containerd OR runc OR crun OR containerd-shim*) OR @ProcessName:(dockerd OR containerd OR runc)) (@process.command_line:(*CAP_SYS_ADMIN* OR *CAP_NET_ADMIN* OR *CAP_SYS_PTRACE* OR *seccomp=unconfined* OR *apparmor=unconfined*) OR @message:(*CAP_SYS_ADMIN* OR *cap_sys_admin* OR *seccomp=unconfined* OR *\"unconfined\"* OR *CapabilityAdd*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 
| ImageFileName=/(dockerd|containerd|runc|crun|containerd-shim)/i 
| regex("(CAP_SYS_ADMIN|CAP_NET_ADMIN|CAP_SYS_PTRACE|cap_sys_admin|seccomp=unconfined|apparmor=unconfined|\"unconfined\")", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Container escape via chroot/nsenter against mounted host filesystem AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts for chroot or nsenter invocations targeting /host, /proc/1/ns, or /proc/1/root — the textbook second-stage of the CVE-2026-44849 chain where the attacker has already created/updated a Swarm service that bind-mounts the host root and now pivots into the host namespace. Targets the executable + flag combinations that distinguish escape from benign chroot use. Rationale: Bound to the specific escape pattern the GHSA describes: 'access the host filesystem from the running container (e.g. via chroot /host)'. Pairs the LOLBin (chroot/nsenter) with the namespace-target tokens so it doesn't match administrative chroot use, and excludes systemd/snapd parents that legitimately invoke chroot during host operations. The advisory text 'chroot /host' is used verbatim as one of the high-signal matches. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/ • https://gtfobins.github.io/gtfobins/chroot/
ATT&CKT1611 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin troubleshooting on a host by chroot'ing into a mounted recovery image
  • Container build pipelines (debootstrap, mkosi) that legitimately chroot into staging directories
  • Container management tools (kubectl debug --target=host, crictl exec) when used by authorised operators
  • Backup / restore tooling mounting host filesystem snapshots for offline inspection
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2", "runc", "crun", "dockerd")
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "debootstrap" and ProcessCommandLine !has "mkosi"
Response runbook
1) Triage: Identify the parent process and container ID (InitiatingProcessParentFileName containerd-shim / runc means it came from a container). Pull `docker ps` / `crictl ps` output and identify the service/task. Correlate with UC1 for the originating Portainer user. 2) Contain: Kill the offending container immediately (`docker kill` / `docker service rm`). Isolate the host from the network — chroot /host implies the attacker now has root on the underlying host. Rotate any credentials cached on the host (/root/.ssh, /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf, cloud metadata creds). 3) Hunt: From the same host, look for outbound C2 (DeviceNetworkEvents), files written under /etc/cron*, /etc/systemd/system, /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, and downstream lateral movement via SSH key reuse. Pivot the source IP of the originating Portainer session against authentication logs.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("chroot", "nsenter")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/host", "/proc/1/ns", "/proc/1/root", "--target 1", "--target=1", "-t 1")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("init", "systemd", "snapd", "snap-confine", "docker-init", "tini")
| where AccountName != "root" or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2", "runc", "crun", "dockerd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessParentCreationTime
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in ("auth", "authpriv", "daemon", "user")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("chroot /host", "chroot=/host", "nsenter --target 1", "nsenter -t 1", "--mount=/proc/1/ns/mnt", "/proc/1/root", "chroot /proc/1/root")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, ProcessID, SyslogMessage, SeverityLevel, HostIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Container Escape via chroot or nsenter to Host Namespace
id: 3c5c9f9a-5f6e-4b6a-9c5a-44849aaa0003
description: Detects chroot or nsenter invoked against /host, /proc/1/ns, or PID-1 mount namespace — the canonical escape from a bind-mounted container.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.t1611
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/chroot'
      - '/nsenter'
  selection_args:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/host'
      - '/proc/1/ns'
      - '/proc/1/root'
      - '--target 1'
      - '--target=1'
      - '-t 1'
  filter_legit:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/systemd'
      - '/snapd'
      - '/snap-confine'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_args and not filter_legit
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) @process.name:(chroot OR nsenter) (@process.command_line:(*/host* OR */proc/1/ns* OR */proc/1/root* OR *--target?1* OR *-t?1*)) -@process.parent.name:(systemd OR snapd OR snap-confine OR docker-init OR tini)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 
| ImageFileName=/\/(chroot|nsenter)$/i 
| regex("(/host|/proc/1/ns|/proc/1/root|--target[= ]1|-t 1)", field=CommandLine) 
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/^(systemd|snapd|snap-confine|docker-init|tini)$/i 
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

Container start with docker.sock or sensitive host-path bind mount AIExploitation High
Hunts for container processes whose runtime spec includes a bind mount of /var/run/docker.sock, /, /root/.ssh, or the Portainer data directory — the post-bypass artefacts of CVE-2026-44849 where a non-admin user has slipped an unrestricted bind mount past the missing AllowBindMountsForRegularUsers check. The docker.sock variant is particularly high-signal because it directly enables sibling-container escape. Rationale: Pulls the exact sensitive paths the advisory enumerates ('bind mounts of any host path, including /, /var/run/docker.sock, SSH keys, or Portainer's own database'). Each of those paths is named verbatim in the Impact section, making the match high-fidelity. docker.sock + a container is sufficient on its own to grant container-breakout primitives, so this also fires as a leading indicator even without confirmed exploitation of CVE-2026-44849. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
ATT&CKT1611 T1613 T1525
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Portainer-agent container itself which legitimately mounts /var/run/docker.sock to manage the local engine
  • CI / build runners (jenkins, gitlab-runner, drone) that mount docker.sock for docker-in-docker builds
  • Observability sidecars (cAdvisor, Sysdig, Datadog agent) that mount docker.sock for container telemetry
  • Watchtower / shepherd-style auto-updaters that legitimately need socket access
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("portainer-agent", "cadvisor", "datadog-agent", "gitlab-runner", "jenkins", "watchtower", "shepherd")
Response runbook
1) Triage: From the container ID, identify the image name and the user who deployed it. Cross-reference with UC1 (was this a non-admin Portainer user calling /services/create or /services/{id}/update?). If image is portainer-agent, cadvisor, datadog-agent, or a known CI runner — likely benign; document and tune. 2) Contain: For unknown / unauthorised containers: `docker kill <id>` then `docker service rm`. Rotate any credentials present at the bind-mount targets (/root/.ssh/* keys, Portainer DB encryption key under /data/portainer). 3) Hunt: Look for child processes from the container that touched docker CLI (sibling container creation), chroot, or nsenter (UC3). Sweep the host for new SSH authorized_keys entries and new cron jobs created since the suspicious container started.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2")
   or FileName in~ ("runc", "crun", "containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/var/run/docker.sock", "docker.sock", "-v /:", "--volume=/:", "source=/ ", "source=/,", "source=/var/run/docker.sock", "/root/.ssh", "/data/portainer", "/host/etc", "\"Source\":\"/\"")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "containerd-shim", "runc", "crun")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/var/run/docker.sock", "docker.sock", "-v /:", "--volume=/:", "source=/ ", "source=/,", "/root/.ssh", "/data/portainer", "\"Source\":\"/\"", "\"Source\":\"/var/run/docker.sock\"")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage, HostIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Docker local-driver volume created with type=none and o=bind (CVE-2026-44849 volume variant) AIExploitation High
Hunts for the volume-driver-bind bypass variant the advisory calls out separately: a Type:volume mount whose VolumeOptions.DriverConfig.Options declares the local driver with type=none and o=bind, or a direct POST /volumes/create with the same payload. Either path materialises a bind-equivalent mount that the partial Mounts struct check never inspected on any Portainer branch. Rationale: Targets the volume-driver-bind variant called out in its own paragraph of the advisory: 'A mount with Type:"volume" and VolumeOptions.DriverConfig.Options: {type:"none", o:"bind", device:"<host path>"} is forwarded to the Docker daemon unchanged'. The triple type=none + o=bind + device= is the canonical local-driver bind incantation; legitimate use of this combination is extremely rare outside of explicit infrastructure-as-code volume declarations on the same host. Also unions in POST /volumes/create on the proxy log because the advisory notes that endpoint never had the AllowBindMountsForRegularUsers check on any branch. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/volume/create/ • https://docs.docker.com/storage/volumes/
ATT&CKT1611 T1078.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Infrastructure-as-Code (Ansible/Terraform/docker-compose) declaring NFS-style local volumes on a build host
  • Stateful application deploys (databases, file servers) that legitimately bind host directories via the local driver pattern
  • Backup tooling that creates short-lived bind-volumes to mount snapshot directories into a restore container
  • Documentation / training environments where the volume-driver bind is being demonstrated
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("docker-compose", "ansible-playbook", "terraform apply", "helm install")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("ansible-playbook", "terraform", "helm")
Response runbook
1) Triage: docker volume inspect the created volume, identify the device= path (the host directory now exposed). If the path is /, /etc, /root, /var/run, or a Portainer data dir, treat as confirmed exploitation. Cross-reference with UC1 to identify the originating Portainer user. 2) Contain: docker volume rm the offending volume (forcing removal of any container using it first). Revoke Swarm-endpoint access for the implicated Portainer user. Apply the workaround from the advisory: block creation of local-driver volumes with type:none / o:bind via a daemon-side allowlist until 2.33.8 / 2.39.2 / 2.41.0 is deployed. 3) Hunt: For any container that mounted the volume, follow UC3 / UC4 — look for chroot/nsenter into the bind target, file writes to sensitive locations on the host, and persistence indicators (cron, systemd units, SSH keys).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dockerd", "docker", "containerd") or FileName in~ ("docker", "dockerd")
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "type=none" and ProcessCommandLine has "o=bind" and ProcessCommandLine has "device=")
     or (ProcessCommandLine has "volume create" and ProcessCommandLine has "--driver local" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-o type=none", "--opt type=none"))
     or (ProcessCommandLine has "VolumeOptions" and ProcessCommandLine has "DriverConfig")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let DockerActivity = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "docker")
    | where (SyslogMessage has "type=none" and SyslogMessage has "o=bind")
         or (SyslogMessage has "\"type\":\"none\"" and SyslogMessage has "\"o\":\"bind\"")
         or (SyslogMessage has "DriverConfig" and SyslogMessage has "\"local\"" and SyslogMessage has "device");
let WebActivity = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csMethod =~ "POST"
    | where csUriStem has "/volumes/create" or csUriStem matches regex @"/services/[^/]+/(create|update)"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csUserName, csUriStem, csMethod;
union isfuzzy=true DockerActivity, WebActivity
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Portainer plugin management API access (CVE-2026-44848) AIExploitation High
Hunts HTTP POST requests to Portainer's /docker/plugins/pull and /docker/plugins/{name}/enable proxy endpoints, which bypass Portainer-side RBAC in vulnerable releases (<2.33.8, <2.39.2, <2.41.0) because /plugins is absent from prefixProxyFuncMap and falls through to executeDockerRequest unauthorized. Rationale: Article identifies the exact vulnerable endpoints (POST /plugins/pull, POST /plugins/{name}/enable) and shows in the Go source excerpt that /plugins is NOT in prefixProxyFuncMap so it bypasses Portainer's authorization wrapper. A successful POST against this URI from a non-admin session is unambiguous exploitation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rrmm-9v76-h3p4
ATT&CKT1190 T1068
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Portainer administrator legitimately installing a Docker volume/log/network plugin from a trusted registry
  • Automation tooling (Ansible/Terraform) using a Portainer admin token to provision plugins after a node rebuild
  • Internal CI/CD pipeline calling the plugin API with a service account during cluster bootstrap
  • Pentest or red-team exercise validating this advisory
  • GET requests from health-check scrapers (excluded by the POST predicate)
Suppression filter
| where csUserName !in~ ("portainer-admin","ansible-portainer","terraform-portainer")
Response runbook
1. Triage: Open the matched proxy/IIS log line and extract csUserName / Portainer JWT subject and source IP; confirm whether that identity holds the Portainer admin role. 2. Contain: Disable the user in Portainer or revoke its Docker-endpoint access, isolate the target Docker host, and quarantine any plugin under /var/lib/docker/plugins/ created within +/- 10 minutes of the request. 3. Hunt: Pivot to host telemetry (UC2/UC3) on the same DeviceName / timestamp window, look for chroot or nsenter from the plugin container, and audit /etc/docker/plugins for new manifests. Upgrade Portainer to 2.33.8 / 2.39.2 / 2.41.0+.

| where csMethod =~ "POST"
| where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/api/endpoints/\d+/docker/plugins/(pull|.+/enable)"
| where scStatus < 400
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csUserName, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Docker plugin runtime spawned from /var/lib/docker/plugins/ on host (CVE-2026-44848) AIInstallation High
Hunts Linux process executions whose binary path begins with /var/lib/docker/plugins/<digest>/rootfs/ and whose parent is dockerd/containerd/runc. Any post-exploit plugin pushed through the unauthorized /plugins/pull + /plugins/{name}/enable chain lands here and executes as root with whatever capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, host bind mounts) the plugin manifest requested. Rationale: Article states 'Docker plugins execute as root on the host' and the Linux runtime path for an enabled plugin is /var/lib/docker/plugins/<digest>/rootfs/. Pairing that image-path prefix with a containerd/dockerd parent yields a near-zero-FP signal because plugin install is normally an admin-only, low-frequency event. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rrmm-9v76-h3p4 • https://docs.docker.com/engine/extend/plugin_api/
ATT&CKT1068 T1611 T1610
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Administrator legitimately installing a known Docker volume plugin (rexray, vieux/sshfs)
  • CI/CD pipeline reinstalling a vetted log driver plugin after a node rebuild
  • Kubernetes CSI plugin operator installing a storage driver
  • Backup software (Velero/Restic) shipping a Docker volume plugin
  • Docker engine upgrade re-creating plugin rootfs paths
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("rexray","vieux/sshfs","docker/telemetry","weaveworks/net-plugin")
Response runbook
1. Triage: Read /var/lib/docker/plugins/<digest>/config.json and inspect for CAP_SYS_ADMIN, propagatedMount, host-path bind mounts, or an untrusted registry origin; correlate with UC1 W3CIISLog/proxy events on the same host+time to identify the Portainer user. 2. Contain: `docker plugin disable <name>` then `docker plugin rm -f <name>`, isolate the host from the network, snapshot for forensics, and rotate any credentials reachable from the host. 3. Hunt: Search the cluster for the same plugin digest, audit other Portainer endpoints accessed by that user, and review auth.log + bash history for chroot/nsenter/mount activity originating from the plugin container.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath startswith "/var/lib/docker/plugins/"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dockerd","containerd","containerd-shim","containerd-shim-runc-v2","runc")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,

| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate

| where ParentProcessName has_any ("dockerd","containerd","containerd-shim","containerd-shim-runc-v2","runc")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Docker daemon plugin install/enable event from non-admin context (CVE-2026-44848) AIInstallation Medium
Surfaces dockerd syslog entries recording plugin pull/install/enable operations. Combined with UC1 (HTTP) and UC2 (process), this is the daemon-side proof of plugin registration and remains useful on hosts that do not run EDR but ship dockerd journald/syslog to the SIEM. Rationale: Article's affected-code excerpt shows requests fall through to executeDockerRequest and are forwarded to dockerd, so the dockerd log is the daemon-side fingerprint of /plugins/pull and /plugins/{name}/enable activity. This UC corroborates UC1+UC2 on hosts without EDR. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rrmm-9v76-h3p4
ATT&CKT1610 T1068
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Admin operator running `docker plugin install` from the CLI for a vetted plugin
  • Docker engine restart replaying plugin-enable events from /var/lib/docker/plugins
  • Swarm rebuild rolling plugins back onto fresh nodes
  • Kubernetes node lifecycle reinstalling logging/storage drivers
  • Plugin upgrade as part of routine patching
Suppression filter
| where PluginName !in~ ("rexray","vieux/sshfs","weaveworks/net-plugin","docker/telemetry")
Response runbook
1. Triage: Extract the plugin name + digest from the dockerd line, list current plugins (`docker plugin ls --no-trunc`), and inspect the manifest for excessive privileges or an unknown registry. 2. Contain: Disable and remove the plugin (`docker plugin disable <name>` then `docker plugin rm -f <name>`), then rotate any credentials accessible from the host. 3. Hunt: Pivot to UC1 (proxy/IIS) by host+timestamp to find which Portainer user triggered the install, and to UC2 to enumerate binaries that ran from /var/lib/docker/plugins.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName in~ ("dockerd","containerd")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/plugins/pull","/plugins/","plugin enabled","plugin pull","plugin install","POST /plugins")
| extend PluginOp = extract(@"plugins?[/=](pull|enable|install)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend PluginName = extract(@"plugin[ =:]([A-Za-z0-9_/.:@-]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| where isnotempty(PluginOp)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, PluginOp, PluginName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.syslog OR docker) @process.name:dockerd (@message:*plugins/pull* OR @message:*"plugin enabled"* OR @message:*"plugin pull"* OR @message:*"plugin install"* OR @message:*"POST /plugins/"*)
ENDPOINT

n8n host inventory hunt — surface vulnerable instances < 1.123.43 / 2.20.7 / 2.22.1 AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunt for hosts running n8n (Node.js parent process or n8n-nodes-base in cmdline) so SOC can cross-reference patched-version state against CVE-2026-44791. This is asset-surface enumeration for the n8n RCE patch bypass — runs read-only and identifies hosts to escalate to vulnerability management. Rationale: Article explicitly names affected packages npm:n8n with version ranges <1.123.43 / 2.20.7 / 2.22.1 and lists NODES_EXCLUDE=n8n-nodes-base.xml as the only workaround. The 'n8n' string in node.exe cmdline is the canonical fingerprint of an n8n instance running on a host — no Defender TVM signature exists for npm packages so process-telemetry is the only practical asset hunt. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/security/advisories/GHSA-hqr4-h3xv-9m3r • https://cybersecuritynews.com/n8n-rce-vulnerabilities/ • https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/security

Contain — for production n8n hosts not yet on a patched release, immediately apply the NODES_EXCLUDE=n8n-nodes-base.xml workaround and restrict workflow create/edit permissions to admin only; schedule emergency upgrade. 3. Hunt — pivot to UC2 to look for any post-exploit shell-spawn evidence on each vulnerable host going back the host's full retention; review n8n credential store for unexpected webhook URLs or executable workflow nodes added since vulnerable version was deployed.

n8n Node.js parent spawning OS shell — post-exploit RCE indicator for CVE-2026-44791 AIExploitation High
Detects the realised RCE outcome of the XML-node prototype-pollution patch bypass: an n8n Node.js process (commandline references n8n / n8n-nodes-base) spawning cmd/powershell/sh/bash with download, base64, reverse-shell, or temp-directory cmdline hallmarks. Article states 'when combined with other nodes, this could lead to RCE on the n8n host' — this catches that exact host-side execution shape. Rationale: Article: 'When combined with other nodes, this could lead to RCE on the n8n host.' n8n runs as a Node.js process; the prototype-pollution → RCE chain manifests as the Node parent spawning an OS shell with attacker-controlled cmdline. Parent fingerprint = node + n8n in cmdline (high-precision asset filter). Child = shell binary. Cmdline tokens = the standard reverse-shell / download cradle vocabulary from public n8n CVE-2026-44789/44790/44791 trio writeups (cross-checked against the CyberSecurityNews coverage that catalogs the trio). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/security/advisories/GHSA-hqr4-h3xv-9m3r • https://cybersecuritynews.com/n8n-rce-vulnerabilities/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.001 T1059.004 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate workflow using n8n's built-in 'Execute Command' node to run `curl https://api.example.com/...` against an approved API
  • n8n container post-deploy startup script invoking `bash -c 'wait-for-it db:5432'`
  • SRE debugging an n8n pod with `kubectl exec -- bash` (parent will be node, child bash, but cmdline is interactive)
  • Backup workflow that pipes data through `base64` for safe transport in a JSON field
  • Workflow that uses `wget` to fetch a CSV from an internal data lake on /tmp scratch
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("wait-for-it","healthcheck","livenessProbe","readinessProbe") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("wait-for-it","--health-cmd","livenessProbe","readinessProbe"))
| where not (ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)curl\s+(-fsSL\s+)?https?://[^ ]*(\.corp\.|\.internal\.|localhost|127\.0\.0\.1)")
Response runbook
1. Triage — pull the exact n8n workflow that triggered the shell spawn (correlate timestamp to n8n execution log on the host; n8n logs workflowId per run) and verify the workflow legitimately contains an Execute Command node performing this action; if no matching workflow exists, treat as confirmed exploitation. 2. Contain — isolate the n8n host from the network, kill node process and any spawned shells, rotate every credential stored in n8n's credential store (DB creds, API keys, webhook secrets), and revoke any active webhook URLs. 3. Hunt — search 30 days back for outbound network connections from node parent process to non-corporate IPs (suspect C2), file writes to /tmp /var/tmp /dev/shm by node, new cron jobs / systemd units / Run-key entries, and any workflow modifications by non-admin n8n users; pivot to other n8n hosts in scope (UC1 inventory) for the same TTP.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("n8n","n8n-nodes-base")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ","Invoke-WebRequest","IEX","Invoke-Expression","base64 ","-EncodedCommand","/tmp/","%TEMP%","bash -i","nc -e","perl -e","python -c")
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)/dev/tcp/"
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\bnc\b.*\b-l\b"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 7d;
let ShellChildren = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh"]);
let SusTokens = dynamic(["curl ","wget ","Invoke-WebRequest","IEX","Invoke-Expression","base64 ","-EncodedCommand","/tmp/","%TEMP%","bash -i","nc -e","perl -e","python -c"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName has "\\node.exe"
  | extend ChildBin = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName,"\\")[-1]))
  | where ChildBin in (ShellChildren)
  | where CommandLine has_any (SusTokens) or CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)/dev/tcp/"
  | where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = TargetUserName,
            ParentCmd = ParentProcessName, ChildImage = NewProcessName, ChildCmd = CommandLine),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
  | where ParentProcessName has "node"
  | where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("n8n","n8n-nodes-base")
  | extend ChildBin = tolower(tostring(split(ActingProcessName,"/")[-1]))
  | where ChildBin in (ShellChildren)
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (SusTokens) or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)/dev/tcp/"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername,
            ParentCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine, ChildImage = ActingProcessName, ChildCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: n8n Node.js Parent Spawning OS Shell with Download or Reverse-Shell Tokens (CVE-2026-44791)

status: experimental
description: Detects post-exploitation of n8n CVE-2026-44791 (XML node prototype pollution patch bypass) where an n8n Node.js parent spawns a shell with download, base64-decode, reverse-shell or temp-directory command-line tokens — the realised RCE outcome.

    - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wrwr-h859-xh2r

n8n workflow API request body containing JS prototype pollution tokens (CVE-2026-44789) AIExploitation High
Hunts for HTTP requests to the n8n workflow/execution API whose body or query string contains JavaScript prototype-pollution sentinels (`__proto__`, `constructor.prototype`, `__defineGetter__`) targeting the HTTP Request node pagination parameter. This is the article-specific pre-exploit signal for CVE-2026-44789. Rationale: Pivots on the exact prototype-pollution sentinels (`__proto__`, `constructor.prototype`, `__defineGetter__`) named in CWE-1321 / GHSA-c8xv-5998-g76h, scoped to the n8n REST/webhook URL surface where the pagination parameter is parsed. Cross-checked against GitHub GHSA advisory, Endor Labs write-up, and Cybersecurity News reporting. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c8xv-5998-g76h • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44789 • https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/ • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1321.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal AppSec / DAST scanners (Burp Suite, Acunetix, Nessus, Nuclei) running prototype-pollution test payloads against n8n instances in dev/staging
  • Legitimate workflow authors saving a workflow whose JSON body literally contains the string `__proto__` (rare but possible in JS-tutorial workflows)
  • Bug-bounty researchers probing public-facing n8n with permission, generating identical telemetry
  • Penetration tests of the n8n perimeter where the same payload list is reused
  • URL-encoded user input in unrelated webhook calls where `%5F` characters happen to align
Suppression filter
| where ClientIP !in ("<scanner-vlan-cidr>") and UA !has_any ("Burp", "Nessus", "Nuclei", "Acunetix", "sqlmap", "ZAP")
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): pull the full HTTP request body and source IP. Confirm whether the URL hits `/rest/workflows`, `/rest/executions`, or `/webhook`; check `User-Agent` and `csUserName` for known scanner signatures or authenticated user identity. Pull n8n version from the host (`npm ls n8n` or container image tag) — confirm version is in vulnerable range (<1.123.43, 2.x <2.20.7, 2.21+ <2.22.1). Step 2 (Contain): if source IP is external and unauthenticated, block at WAF/reverse proxy. If authenticated, force-revoke the user's API tokens, suspend account, and snapshot the n8n DB for forensics. Disable the HTTP Request node via `NODES_EXCLUDE=n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest` until upgrade lands. Step 3 (Hunt): pivot on the n8n host AID — look for `node.exe`/`node` spawning `cmd.exe`, `sh`, `powershell.exe`, or LOLBins in the following 60 minutes; check `AsepValueUpdate` / cron for persistence; review egress to non-org IPs from the n8n host.

let PollutionTokens = dynamic(["__proto__", "constructor.prototype", "__defineGetter__", "prototype[", "%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F", "%5Fproto%5F"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemotePort in (5678, 443, 80) or LocalPort in (5678, 443, 80)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("node.exe", "n8n.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "n8n"
| where RemoteUrl has_any (PollutionTokens)
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (PollutionTokens)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, LocalPort, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let PollutionTokens = dynamic(["__proto__", "constructor.prototype", "__defineGetter__", "prototype[", "%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F", "%5Fproto%5F"]);
let IISHits = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where csUriStem has_any ("/rest/workflows", "/rest/executions", "/webhook")
    | where csUriQuery has_any (PollutionTokens) or csUriStem has_any (PollutionTokens)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, ClientIP = cIP, User = csUserName,
              Method = csMethod, Uri = csUriStem, Query = csUriQuery, UA = csUserAgent,
              Source = "W3CIISLog";
let CSLHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RequestURL has_any ("/rest/workflows", "/rest/executions", "/webhook")
    | where RequestURL has_any (PollutionTokens) or Message has_any (PollutionTokens)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DestinationHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP,

              Query = RequestContext, UA = RequestClientApplication,
              Source = "CommonSecurityLog";
let WebHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where Url has_any ("/rest/workflows", "/rest/executions", "/webhook")
    | where Url has_any (PollutionTokens) or UrlOriginal has_any (PollutionTokens)

description: Detects HTTP requests to n8n workflow/execution/webhook API endpoints whose URI or query string carries JavaScript prototype-pollution sentinel tokens used to exploit CVE-2026-44789 in the HTTP Request node pagination handler.
references:

  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44789

detection:
  selection_uri:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/rest/workflows'
      - '/rest/executions'
      - '/webhook'
  selection_payload:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - '__proto__'
      - 'constructor.prototype'
      - '__defineGetter__'
      - 'prototype['
      - '%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F'
  condition: selection_uri and selection_payload
falsepositives:
  - JavaScript prototype-pollution scanners (Burp, Acunetix, Nessus) run by internal security teams
  - Legitimate developer use of `__proto__` as a literal string in a workflow body (rare)
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:aws.alb OR source:cloudflare) (@http.url:(*"/rest/workflows"* OR *"/rest/executions"* OR *"/webhook"*) OR @url:(*"/rest/workflows"* OR *"/rest/executions"* OR *"/webhook"*)) (@http.url:(*__proto__* OR *constructor.prototype* OR *__defineGetter__* OR *%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F*) OR @url:(*__proto__* OR *constructor.prototype* OR *__defineGetter__*) OR @http.url_details.queryString:(*__proto__* OR *constructor.prototype*))

Post-exploit RCE: node.js (n8n) spawning shell or scripting interpreter AIInstallation High
Detects the post-exploitation tail of CVE-2026-44789 — the n8n `node` process spawning a shell (`cmd.exe`, `sh`, `bash`, `powershell.exe`) or a LOLBin. Prototype-pollution RCEs land here because the polluted global lets the attacker reroute child-process spawning into arbitrary commands run as the n8n service account. Rationale: Uses the most reliable post-exploit signal — n8n's `node` process spawning a shell or LOLBin — which is the actual outcome chain described in GHSA-c8xv-5998-g76h ("combined with other techniques this could lead to RCE"). Article + Endor Labs corroboration both flag RCE as the impact, and CWE-1321 prototype-pollution chains universally land via hijacked child-process spawn. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c8xv-5998-g76h • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44789 • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1321.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1059 T1059.001 T1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate use of the n8n Execute Command node (`n8n-nodes-base.executeCommand`) by an authorised workflow — verify the workflow owner and content
  • n8n custom community nodes that legitimately invoke `curl`/`wget` for file fetching
  • Node-based CI/CD agents running on the same host that spawn shells for build tasks
  • Diagnostic / troubleshooting scripts where an admin manually exec'd into the n8n container and ran `sh`
  • Docker entrypoint chains where the n8n container's `node` PID 1 spawns `sh -c` for shutdown handling
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "n8n-nodes-base.executeCommand") and not (DeviceName has_any ("build-", "ci-", "jenkins-")) and not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "docker-entrypoint")
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): pull the parent `node` command line and the child cmd line — confirm the parent is n8n (check folder path for `/n8n/`, `.n8n`, or `n8n-nodes-base`). Pull the n8n version via `npm ls n8n` or container image tag; confirm vulnerable range. Check whether the workflow that spawned the shell is documented to use the Execute Command node. Step 2 (Contain): isolate the n8n host via Defender / Falcon Real-Time Response. Kill the child process tree. Rotate the n8n encryption key (`N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY`) and DB credentials. If the host is internet-facing, take it off the load balancer. Step 3 (Hunt): retrospectively search the n8n web logs over the previous 30 days for the prototype-pollution URI patterns from UC1; inventory all workflows for unexpected Execute Command nodes; correlate against `AsepValueUpdate` for new persistence and outbound `DnsRequest` / `NetworkConnectIP4` from the n8n host to non-org infrastructure.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let ShellsAndLolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","zsh","dash","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","nc","ncat","socat"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("n8n", "\\n8n\\", "/n8n/")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("n8n", "\\.n8n\\")
| where FileName in~ (ShellsAndLolbins)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let ShellsAndLolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","zsh","dash","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","nc","ncat","socat"]);
let WinHits = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node\\","\\node")
    | where tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]) in~ (ShellsAndLolbins)
    | where (CommandLine has_any ("n8n")) or (ParentProcessName has "n8n") or true
    | where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, User=TargetUserName,
              ParentImage=ParentProcessName, ChildImage=NewProcessName,
              ChildCmd=CommandLine, Source="SecurityEvent";
let AsimHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (ShellsAndLolbins) or TargetProcessName has_any (ShellsAndLolbins)
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=ActorUsername,
              ParentImage=ParentProcessName, ChildImage=coalesce(TargetProcessName, ActingProcessName),
              ChildCmd=coalesce(TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessCommandLine),
              Source="ImProcessCreate";
union isfuzzy=true WinHits, AsimHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc
